judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard identification preamble; the only oddity is 'by and among' used for two parties, which changes nothing about meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines the 'Parties' as only Licensee and Clearwire, yet Sections 5.01, 6.01 and 6.02 make representations to and by 'Clearwire Parent' and Section 4.02(c)(iii) refers to 'each Clearwire Affiliate that is a Party hereto', a latent incoherence about who is bound.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recital language such as 'the bundle of value ... is central' and 'would not have been executed but for all of the elements of the Total Consideration' is purposive rather than operative and invites argument about the deal's essential consideration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recitals define 'Total Consideration' as EBS Economic Royalties plus Access Right Royalties, while the operative Articles II and III speak of 'Prepaid Royalties' refundable in full under Sections 2.02 and 9.01 — a classic recital-versus-operative tension about whether the $23,000,000 was earned consideration or a refundable advance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A descriptive overview that mainly creates the defined term 'EBS Spectrum Capacity'; the parenthetical 'when under IUA hereunder' is slightly clumsy but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Sections 1.02(a)-(b) and 4.01 without visible contradiction, though the defined term it creates is used loosely elsewhere (e.g. 'EBS Spectrum' in Section 7.06).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Exceeds the value of the Initial Spectrum Capacity' and the tripartite characterisation of the payment (Option consideration, ROFR consideration, advance payment) are vague about how much of the $23,000,000 is attributable to each.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states part of the payment is consideration for the Option and ROFR, whereas Section 2.02 requires refund of the entire unapplied Prepaid Royalties Balance and Section 9.01 repeats that on any termination — a genuine conflict over whether any of the payment was non-refundable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Which consists of, among other items' introduces four enumerated rights followed by an open catch-all ('technology, facilities, equipment and other functionality'), leaving the reach of the Access Right Royalties uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The list overlaps but does not match Article III's contents (it omits the MVNO and equipment rights of Sections 3.05-3.07), a mismatch a court could have to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Typographically corrupted ('TUA', 'm the manner', 'n ARTICLE II') but the sense is recoverable; it simply defines Access Right Royalties by reference to Article III.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It labels the Article III bundle 'Access Right Royalties' while Section 1.01(c) and the recitals use the same term for a differently composed bundle, a modest definitional inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Option turns on undefined-in-text 'Available' spectrum and on prices 'to be negotiated in good faith based on fair market value' subject to a $0.15 cap — an agreement to agree whose enforceability and mechanics are contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its interaction with Section 1.04 (ROFR applies unless the Option Notice was complied with), Section 1.02(d) (options lapse at Term end) and Section 9.03 (options survive) creates real reconciliation work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Riddled with defects: 'a GSA the covers the same metropolitan are in Puerto Rico' as the definition of 'Substantially Similar', an MFN mechanism with a $0.15 ceiling and a $0.10 floor, and a parenthetical example doing definitional work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The twelve-month post-Term MFN survival sits awkwardly with Section 9.01's Term, Section 1.02(d)'s lapse rule and Section 2.02's refund trigger, and the price floor conflicts with the Section 1.02(b) negotiation regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It repeats verbatim the exercise sentence of Section 1.02(b) and then carves out Puerto Rico 'without regard to the earlier expiration of the Term', an awkward but intelligible qualification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Any outstanding Options shall lapse automatically upon the expiration of the Term' sits directly against Section 9.03, which preserves Option and ROFR rights whose triggering event occurred (or would have occurred) before expiration, and against Section 2.02's proviso that the Term is not deemed expired while Option periods run.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Jointly and severally liable therefore' (for 'therefor') is a spelling slip that does not change meaning; the obligation to cause a non-signatory affiliate to assume duties is clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates 'Collateral Documents' to be executed later, which sits in mild tension with the integration clause in Section 10.03, but nothing squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening carve-out ('unless (1) ... and (2) the ROFR Offer does not call for payment of a lower price, or other terms that are more favorable to the third party') is convoluted and its double negative is genuinely hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Section 1.02(b) and to 'arbitration under this Agreement', but the arbitration machinery in Section 10.11 is truncated/unspecified, and Section 1.02(d)'s automatic lapse rule complicates the ROFR Period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite payment obligation of a fixed sum on a fixed date; nothing in it is genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Prepaid Royalties are applied 'as provided in Section 1.02(b)', which by its terms addresses only Future Spectrum Capacity, yet this Section applies them to Initial Spectrum Capacity IUAs too; it is also the sum whose refundability Sections 1.01(b), 2.02 and 9.01 treat differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso that 'the Term shall not be deemed to have expired for this purpose' while Option periods run, coupled with Clearwire's unilateral power to extend the refund date and thereby extend the Term, is circular and hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with Section 9.01, under which the Term ends on the earliest of eighteen months, exhaustion of the Prepaid Royalties, or the very refund this Section requires — so the refund both ends the Term and is triggered by the Term ending.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Commercially reasonable best efforts' to 'consider' entering a joint venture, and the benchmark of provision 'in a manner consistent with' third-party agreements, are vague standards whose content is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes exercise of the Option for Licensee PR Spectrum under Section 1.02(c) and a wholesale price benchmark that also appears in Section 3.05(a), but no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence pointer to Sections 3.02-3.04 with no operative content of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Sections 3.03 and 3.04, which it merely cross-references.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The highest level of premium mass market retail service' and 'fully portable ... to the extent that Clearwire offers such portability to any customer' are moving, vague benchmarks, and the subordination to Clearwire's 'then generally applicable Acceptable Use Policy' is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is incorporated by Section 3.05(a) for MVNO accounts and by Sections 3.03-3.04, and the AUP subordination is expressly made subject to the rest of the Agreement, so no square conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In such locations ... on a full time basis as Licensee desires' is broad, and the obligation to 'jointly approach the FCC' before invoking dispute resolution is a soft condition precedent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It invokes 'the Dispute Resolution Procedure' while Section 10.11 defines 'Dispute Resolution Procedures' and the text of that Section is incomplete, so the referenced machinery cannot be located in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Adjusted upward every five years proportionate to the growth of the overall data capacity ... as measured by its average throughput' leaves the measurement method expressly unagreed, and 'in such fashion as shall be agreed' is an agreement to agree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers to 'arbitration' for measurement disputes while Section 10.11's dispute machinery is truncated, and its five-year adjustment cycle sits against Section 3.04(a)'s annual January 31 recalculation of a partially overlapping account entitlement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short chapeau; 'in addition to, and not in lieu of' is clear language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It characterises the Section 3.03 accounts as provided 'pursuant to the Educational Reservation', whereas Section 3.03(b)'s Basic accounts are a separate Clearwire deliverable, a small mismatch in how the two entitlements stack.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The greater-of formula uses 'Sector', a term not defined in the visible text, and 'Licensee's Market Area' is used without definition alongside 'the Market Area where Licensee holds an FCC License'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annual recalculation as of January 31 must be squared with Section 3.03(b)'s five-year adjustment and with Section 3.04(b)'s delivery trigger at commercial launch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula is arithmetically specified, though 'rounded up or down to the nearest whole number' and 'substantially overlapping GSAs' leave some play at the edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The inputs depend on 'Market Area' and on channels 'under a use agreement with Clearwire', concepts used consistently elsewhere in Article III.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rule says accounts are 'not for resale' yet the parenthetical example expressly permits a university to 'resell the service to its students', and 'officially associated' is a vague boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The no-resale rule must be read with Section 3.05's MVNO resale right and Section 3.08(b)'s resale prohibition with cross-referenced exceptions, a set of provisions that do not sit perfectly together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A timing rule keyed to commercial launch or the Commencement Date, whichever is later; clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'this Section 3.04(b)' within itself and depends on 'Commencement Date' defined in the IUA rather than here, a minor external dependency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The lowest wholesale rate provided by Clearwire to an arms-length third party in such Market Area or other comparable market' is a vague benchmark, and 'other comparable market' has no boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.01 contemplates a Puerto Rico joint venture only if services are purchased 'at greater than Clearwire's lowest wholesale price', which pulls against this Section's lowest-rate entitlement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Provided to any Licensee requesting the right' uses a plural-licensee formulation in a two-party agreement, and 'thirty (30) days after the availability of such services' does not say availability of what, to whom.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It subordinates a 'standard Clearwire wholesale agreement form' to this Agreement and the IUA, consistent with Section 1.03's Collateral Documents concept.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '10% above Clearwire's cost to acquire' is a definite formula, though 'cost to acquire' could be argued over; 'used solely by Educational End Users and not for resale' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The no-resale rule mirrors Sections 3.04(a)(ii) and 3.08(b), whose resale carve-outs are not repeated here — a small inconsistency across the equipment and service provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As contemplated by their agreement' has no clear referent in a two-party clause, and 'reasonably necessary support made available to Clearwire's commercial customers generally' is doubly vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Section 3.08(a)'s Preferred Content Provider access rights and is qualified by Section 3.08(c)'s capacity reservation, but nothing squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Premium third party content providers' is an undefined comparator class, so the content of the 'same degree of access' benchmark is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.08(c) expressly lets Clearwire restrict these very capabilities, and Section 3.07 grants overlapping access, so the two must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Clearwire's most favored program suppliers' and 'equal features and/or service sets' are undefined comparators, and 'educational in nature' is a vague content restriction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its resale prohibition is expressly excepted only by Sections 3.04(a)(ii) and 3.05, which does not obviously cover the Section 3.09 reciprocity channel or Section 3.06 equipment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No longer commercially and technically feasible due to limitations in network capabilities' is a vague, self-judged trigger for a unilateral cut-back right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The direction that 'Clearwire shall comply with the provisions of ARTICLE III' is a circular self-reference (this clause is in Article III) and no Article III provision actually addresses information about capacity usage, and the cut-back power pulls against the Section 3.08(a) and 3.07 access grants.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Commercially reasonable best efforts' blends two different standards, and 'one ordinary unpaid channel carried on such entity's basic tier' plus 'incremental out-of-pocket costs ... exclusively for the benefit of Licensee' leave real definitional gaps.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is one of the Access Right Royalties listed in Section 1.01(c), and nothing else in the instrument contradicts the best-efforts-only nature of the commitment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line chapeau; the only slip is 'required of it' for two parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsections (a) through (c) exist and are consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Each a Wire Account' is plural drafting for a single account, and 'Absent notice of different instructions' is loose, but the delivery list is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It references Schedule 4.01, Schedule A and Exhibit III (Stock Pledge Agreement), all of which appear in the exhibit/schedule lists though not in the text supplied.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short delivery list; 'the Upfront Royalty provided for in the applicable EBS Spectrum Capacity IUA as reflected on Schedule A' introduces a term used nowhere else in the body.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.01 requires payment of $23,000,000 in 'Prepaid Royalties' on execution, while this Section requires delivery of an 'Upfront Royalty' per IUA at the same moment — the relationship between the two payments is not spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional officers' certificate requirement, definite in content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the certificate conditions in Sections 4.02(c)(ii)(2) and (iii)(2); the reference to a 'board of directors' for a Nevada LLC is a minor mismatch with Section 6.01.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple statement that the Initial Closing occurs on the Effective Date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Sections 4.01 and 4.03, although the table of contents numbers this Section 4.03 rather than 4.02.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall take place as specified in the applicable IUAs when the Parties reach agreement on the pricing' makes the closing contingent on a future agreement, which is indefinite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Section 1.02(b) negotiation regime, which may never produce agreement, and its Subsequent Closing Date feeds the survival period in Section 10.02.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The condition is a sentence fragment — 'No temporary restraining order ... preventing the consummation' with no verb such as 'shall be in effect' — a grammatical defect in the operative condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the party-specific conditions in the following subsections and conflicts with nothing else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard bring-down and certificate conditions, waivable only in writing by Clearwire; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires certification of IUA representations rather than the Article V representations, a slight disconnect with Article V but nothing contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mislabelled '(ii)' when it is the third subsection (the preceding Clearwire conditions are also '(ii)'), a numbering error that Section 8.03-style cross-references could compound.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires resolutions of 'each Clearwire Affiliate that is a Party hereto', although the preamble identifies only two Parties and no Clearwire Affiliate signs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says all Closings occur by electronic delivery and then, in the same sentence, that the Initial Closing occurs at a law firm's offices — an internal tension in a single short provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Agreement addresses closing location, so the tension is confined to this provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable best efforts' and 'necessary, proper or advisable' are boilerplate standards, vague but of a kind courts routinely apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside the 'commercially reasonable efforts' standard in Section 7.01 and 'commercially reasonable best efforts' in Sections 3.09 and 7.07, an inconsistent efforts vocabulary across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard organisation and good standing representation with a materiality carve-out; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relies on 'Licensee Material Adverse Effect', defined only in the Exhibit I definitions not reproduced here, but is otherwise consistent with Article VIII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional authority and enforceability representation; the equitable-principles qualification is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines 'Transactions' and 'Licensee Documents' used in Sections 5.03, 5.06 and 10.01 without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-conflict representation; the clause numbering is garbled by OCR but the structure is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mirror of Section 6.03(a) and consistent with the Schedule 5.03 exception mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The blanket 'no consent ... is required' representation is subject only to the open-ended catch-all 'except as contemplated herein or therein', whose reach is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its mirror, Section 6.03(b), expressly carves out FCC spectrum lease applications, and Sections 7.03-7.05 assume FCC involvement throughout, so the unqualified Licensee representation is hard to square with the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Nor does there exist any basis therefore' and the exception for 'immaterial claims brought ... in the ordinary course of business' are vague, and 'therefore' is a misspelling of 'therefor'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves out 'FCC Proceedings' consistently with the FCC-centric covenants in Article VII; no conflict is apparent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says Licensee 'has complied in all respects' and then immediately excepts noncompliance without a Material Adverse Effect, and the whole is prefaced by 'only to the best knowledge' and an assumption about third parties' compliance — layered qualifications that fight each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.02 strips out knowledge and materiality qualifiers when computing Damages, which materially changes the effect of this heavily qualified representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, absolute brokers representation with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section 6.06 and conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines 'best knowledge' circularly ('is made to its best knowledge after commercially reasonable investigation') and 'commercially reasonable investigation' is itself undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.04 uses plain 'knowledge of Licensee' while Sections 5.05 uses 'best knowledge', and only the latter is defined here, leaving the standard for the former unstated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard organisation representation; the only oddity is calling an LLC 'duly qualified ... as a foreign corporation'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes representations about Clearwire Parent, which the preamble does not name as a Party, and Section 6.03 by contrast omits Clearwire Parent entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional authority representation; 'board of directors' language for an LLC is a small mismatch but not meaning-changing here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has Clearwire Parent representing authority and defines 'Clearwire Documents' collectively, yet the binding-obligation sentence covers only Clearwire, and Clearwire Parent is not a signatory under the preamble.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-conflict representation with a Material Adverse Effect carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Unlike Sections 6.01 and 6.02 it omits Clearwire Parent, an inconsistency across Article VI, though a minor one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear no-consents representation with a specific, identified FCC filing exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 6.05's identical carve-out and with the FCC framework of Article VII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It uses a bespoke qualifier — effect 'on the ability of Clearwire to close hereunder' — rather than Clearwire Material Adverse Effect, but the meaning is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The differing materiality qualifier from the parallel Licensee representation in Section 5.04 is an asymmetry, not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Has complied in all respects' immediately qualified by a Material Adverse Effect exception is internally awkward, and the trailing FCC exception is bolted on after a stray double comma.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the carve-out in Section 6.03(b) and mirrors Section 5.05; no direct conflict emerges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short absolute brokers representation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section 5.06 without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reciprocal 'commercially reasonable efforts' obligations over a long enumerated list ending in 'permits and licenses'; the standard is vague but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The efforts standard differs from Section 4.04's 'reasonable best efforts' and Section 7.07's 'commercially reasonable best efforts', an inconsistency in vocabulary rather than substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger — a matter the notifying party itself 'determines is reasonably likely to constitute a breach' — is subjective and effectively self-policing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imposes an obligation on Clearwire Parent, which the preamble does not make a Party, repeating the Clearwire Parent problem seen in Sections 6.01-6.02.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence stacks two provisos that partly cancel the covenant, and 'creates a material risk that Licensee shall lose any FCC Qualification' is a vague standard, as is the scope limiter 'spectrum that has not been subject to an IUA'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The opening limitation to non-IUA spectrum is hard to reconcile with the same sentence's reference to 'Clearwire's obligation to cause Licensee's FCC License to timely meet the substantial service requirement', an obligation that arises under the IUAs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The consent regime ('reasonably acceptable to Clearwire') is followed by a 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' sentence permitting assignment of the whole Agreement to affiliates without consent — the two sentences address different objects and their interaction is genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Free affiliate assignment sits against Section 1.04, which extends the ROFR to Spectrum held by Licensee's Affiliates, and against Section 10.09's 'permitted assigns'; the section's opening limitation to non-IUA spectrum compounds the problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Parties believe that the provisions of this Agreement comply with all current FCC rules' is a statement of belief given operative force by an agreement 'not to express any contrary view to regulatory agencies or the general public', a covenant of uncertain scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits uneasily with Section 3.03(a)'s contemplation that the Parties may jointly approach the FCC for clarification of disagreements about the Educational Reservation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All fees and taxes (now existing or hereafter arising) imposed on Licensee as a result of the licensing, regulation or use' is a broad general obligation followed by an enumerated 'including, without limitation' list, leaving the catch-all's reach contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its duration ('until the end of the term of the IUA that is the last to expire') outruns the eighteen-month Term in Section 9.01, and it overlaps Section 10.01's separate tax allocation, requiring reconciliation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Act in a cooperative manner to preserve the intent of the relationships ... to their mutual advantage' with 'commercially reasonable best efforts' is an aspirational obligation with no ascertainable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against the specific, bargained allocations in Articles I-III, such an open-ended good-faith covenant could be argued to expand or override them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (iii) indemnifies for anything 'otherwise related to the activities of Clearwire, any of its Affiliates or any of its sublicensees or resellers including, without limitation, damage to health' — an unbounded catch-all with a single odd specific example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Licensee-side indemnity in Section 8.01(a) has no equivalent operational limb, and Section 8.03's deductible is expressed only for the (i) limbs, leaving (iii) uncapped.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in 'statutory or regulatory compliance requirements' and items 'of every kind and description, contingent or otherwise', with no exclusion for consequential damages.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its materiality-stripping sentence deliberately overrides the Material Adverse Effect qualifiers in Articles V and VI, which is intentional but sets up a tension a party could exploit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is captioned and framed as a limit on representation-and-warranty claims, yet its text also reaches 'the breach of any covenant', and it cross-refers to 'Section 8.01(a)(i)' when Section 8.01(a)'s limbs are labelled (a) and (i) — a live mechanical and scope defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Covenant breaches are indemnified under Sections 8.01(a)(ii) and 8.01(b)(ii), which this deductible does not cite, so whether covenant claims bear the $10,000 threshold cannot be answered from the instrument as a whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but conventional claims procedure; 'reasonably and promptly' and 'reasonably satisfactory' are ordinary standards courts apply routinely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly operates 'regardless of the Deductible referred to above', harmonising with Section 8.03, and Section 8.04(c) softens the notice requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical notice-of-sums provision with no payment deadline stated, but nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It follows naturally from Section 8.04(a) and conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actual loss and prejudice' is a standard prejudice requirement; the provision is short and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the notice obligation in Section 8.04(a) consistently rather than contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Term ends on the earliest of three events, one of which (return of the unused Prepaid Royalties) is itself triggered by the Term ending, making the definition circular; 'except as it pertains to Puerto Rico' is undefined, and 'Title 7 or 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code' misdescribes chapters as titles.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely collides with Section 2.02, which both requires refund within five days of expiration and lets Clearwire extend the refund date and thereby extend the Term, and with Section 1.02(d)'s automatic lapse of Options versus Section 9.03's survival of them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Event of Default' is confined to failures 'in circumstances where such failure results in the inability of the other party to exercise its full rights', an unusually narrow and vague trigger, and the second sentence about a 'Loss' has nothing to do with defaults.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The narrow default definition is the gateway to termination under Section 9.01(ii)-(iii), so it limits remedies that Section 10.10 declares cumulative and non-exclusive, and it imports 'Loss' from an IUA not before the court.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Obligations that by their nature would continue' is the usual vague survival formula, and the parenthetical 'or would have occurred, if Licensee complied in full' creates a counterfactual trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves Option and ROFR rights past expiration, which is difficult to reconcile with Section 1.02(d)'s statement that outstanding Options 'shall lapse automatically upon the expiration of the Term' except where prior notice was given.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of transfer-type taxes closing with 'or similar fees or taxes or governmental charges', a catch-all whose reach against the specifics is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 'Licensee(s) Indemnified Parties' where Section 8.01(b) defines 'Licensee Indemnified Parties', and it overlaps the broader tax obligation in Section 7.06 with a different duration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All agreements and covenants ... shall survive indefinitely until, by their respective terms, they are no longer operative' is self-cancelling wording, and 'indefinitely until' is internally contradictory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The one-year survival of representations must be reconciled with Section 9.03's general survival rule and with the indemnity in Section 8.01, which is not expressly time-limited.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional integration, amendment and non-waiver language; the requirement of a writing 'making specific reference to this Agreement' is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement expressly contemplates IUAs, Collateral Documents (Section 1.03) and a standard wholesale agreement (Section 3.05(b)) as separate instruments, so the 'entire understanding' claim requires harmonising with those documents and with Schedule A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard New York governing-law clause with an express conflicts-of-law exclusion; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contains no forum selection, leaving Section 10.11's truncated dispute-resolution machinery to do that work, but there is no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional headings clause, definite in effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Given the numbering mismatches between the table of contents and the body (e.g. Section 4.02 versus 4.03), this clause actually resolves rather than creates incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Deemed given when delivered personally or by overnight courier, or mailed by certified mail' is ambiguous as to whether mailed notices are effective on mailing or on receipt, and the addressee block names 'Clearwire Spectrum Holdings I LLC' rather than II.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Numerous provisions turn on notice timing (Sections 1.02(b), 1.04's thirty- and fifteen-day windows, 7.03's five days, 9.01's cure periods), so the effectiveness ambiguity propagates through the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent possible' and 'reasonable time to comment' are soft, but the consent requirement and the legal-requirement exception are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Sections 11.14-11.15 on confidentiality listed in the table of contents but absent from the text, so its relationship to the confidentiality regime cannot be fully checked.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An unusually bare severability clause with no reformation language and no carve-out for provisions going to the essence of the bargain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital that 'the IUAs and this Agreement would not have been executed but for all of the elements of the Total Consideration' pulls directly against a rule that the balance survives however central the excised term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading promises 'Assignment' but the text says only that the Agreement binds 'successors and permitted assigns' without stating what an assignment permits or prohibits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether an assignment is 'permitted' can only be answered from Section 7.04, which addresses FCC licence assignments and free affiliate transfers and expressly applies 'only to spectrum that has not been subject to an IUA' — leaving the Agreement without a general assignment rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The stipulation that 'monetary damages alone will not be adequate' followed by entitlement to specific performance 'in addition to ... including money damages' is conventional but internally cross-cutting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'Notwithstanding any other provision herein' cumulative-remedies rule pulls against Section 10.11(a), which makes the Dispute Resolution Procedures 'their sole means of' resolving disputes, and against Section 9.02's narrow default definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision breaks off mid-sentence at 'as their sole means of', so the exclusivity it purports to create has no stated object — a defect visible on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An exclusive dispute mechanism is hard to reconcile with Section 10.10's cumulative remedies and specific performance, with Section 3.03(a)'s FCC-first procedure, and with the arbitration references in Sections 1.04 and 3.03(b).
